messages:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT P2 — sierra-prod (VPC) seeing elevated 5xx rate on dedicated pool dpool-9. Affected endpoints: /generate, /chat. Error rate ~27% for last 10m. Pager: @Emma (on-call). Please ack and triage. Link: https://infra.redwood/incident/2161234567

Emma (on-call): Acked. jumping in. starting a quick impact check and logs. tagging Raj and Marta.

Raj P.: I see repeated model swap failures in the runtime logs. It looks like when the pool falls back to the quantized safe variant, some requests time out and then requeue, causing backpressure. Snip from logs:

```
2026-03-15T05:42:01Z runtime: serve request tenant=sierra-prod route=/generate model=redwood/s3-v3.2 fallback=quantized-safe status=500 err="kv-cache-miss + retry-exhausted"
2026-03-15T05:42:02Z runtime: model-switch tenant=sierra-prod from=redwood/s3-v3.3 -> to=redwood/s3-v3.2-quantized reason=capacity_pressure
2026-03-15T05:42:04Z runtime: serve request tenant=sierra-prod route=/chat model=redwood/s3-v3.2-quantized status=504 err="inference-timeout"
```

Raj P.: baseline: traffic spike + fallback oscillation. Suspect policy that allows automatic swap to quantized variant is too aggressive for this tenant's dedicated pool.

Marta S. (SRE): Agreed. For dedicated/VPC tenants we should be conservative with automatic safe-variant fallbacks. Immediate mitigation: pin the tenant's runtime to a stable safe model variant (redwood/s3-v3.2-safe) on dpool-9 and disable automatic fallback for that tenant for the next 3 hours while we stabilize. Also propose a gradual canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) for the pinned variant if we need to roll any change.

Marta S. (SRE): Suggested admin command to pin model (run from infra-admin host):

```
# pin model for tenant in dedicated pool
redwood tenant model pin \
  --tenant sierra-prod \
  --pool dpool-9 \
  --model redwood/s3-v3.2-safe \
  --until 3h \
  --reason "mitigation: reduce fallback thrash, stabilize latency/errors"
```

Lia C. (CSE): Customer impact notes from Sierra support: billing assistant started returning truncated invoices and timeouts around 05:30Z, customers saw delays of 5-12s and occasional 500s. They flagged this as high (affecting revenue flows). Lia: Sierra ops on standby, prefer if we do mitigation with prior notice but will accept emergency pin as immediate fix.

oncall-bot: runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/tenant-fallbacks — follow the dedicated-pool pin checklist, step 3 = snapshot caches + warm.

Raj P.: Before pinning, snapshot KV cache so we can warm safe variant after pin (avoids cold-start failcases). Use internal snapshot endpoint:

```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/snapshot-kv \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"sierra-prod","pool":"dpool-9","target_model":"redwood/s3-v3.2-safe"}'
```

Marta S. (SRE): Note: snapshot+warm will increase CPU for ~30s. We'll schedule during mitigation window. Also create a temporary rule to prevent auto-fallback:

```
# disallow automatic variant fallback for tenant
redwood tenant config set \
  --tenant sierra-prod \
  --pool dpool-9 \
  --key routing.allow_auto_fallback \
  --value false
```

Emma (on-call): Performing pin + snapshot now. I'll run the two commands and start a 5% canary. Posting progress.

Emma (on-call): Ran snapshot -> response jobId=job-33421. Pin command executed, response: ok, pin active until 3h. Starting canary at 5%.

```
# canary rollout config
{
  "tenant": "sierra-prod",
  "pool": "dpool-9",
  "model": "redwood/s3-v3.2-safe",
  "canary": {
    "steps": [5, 25, 100],
    "interval_seconds": 600
  }
}
```

DeployBot: CANARY STARTED — rollout-id=roll-216123-a1. Canary 5% started at 05:46:30Z. Metrics: error_rate=8% (down from 27%), median latency=420ms. Link: https://console.redwood/rollouts/roll-216123-a1

Lia C. (CSE): Told Sierra ops that we pinned and started canary. They appreciate the immediate action. They asked that we do not flush their persistent KV workspace; only warm. Confirmed with customer to keep snapshot for roll-back.

Marta S. (SRE): Monitoring notes: create a short alert for regression during canary: if error_rate increases >2x baseline or latency >1500ms, abort and rollback. Also prepare rollback cmd:

```
redwood tenant model unpin --tenant sierra-prod --pool dpool-9 --reason "rollback"
```

Raj P.: Observing request traces — upstream timeouts reduced, no retry storms so far. We'll keep watch on memory & GPU queue length.

Emma (on-call): Canary at 5% healthy after 12m. Error rate steady ~6-9%. Proceeding to 25% in 10m window unless objections.

Marta S. (SRE): No objections. Proceed.

DeployBot: Canary step -> 25% complete at 05:58:00Z. Metrics: error_rate=4.3%, p95 latency=740ms.

Emma (on-call): Rolling to 100% now per rollout plan.

DeployBot: Rollout COMPLETE at 06:08:12Z. rollout-id=roll-216123-a1. Final metrics: error_rate=1.2%, median latency=410ms. Pin remains active until 3h.

Lia C. (CSE): Sierra ops confirmed degraded behavior stopped and billing flows back to normal. They want a follow-up within the hour to discuss permanent config changes.

Marta S. (SRE): Post-incident actions:
- Add tenant-level default: conservative fallback thresholds for dedicated pools.
- Update runbook to require cache snapshot before any auto-variant swap for VPC tenants.
- Engineering task: improve stability of automatic fallback heuristics (ENG-RUNTIME ticket created).

Emma (on-call): Handoff to Raj for overnight watch. Summary for next on-call:
- What I did: pinned sierra-prod to redwood/s3-v3.2-safe on dpool-9, disabled auto-fallback, snapshot/warmed KV caches, executed canary to 100%.
- Current state: pinned, metrics healthy (error_rate ~1.2%).
- Next steps: monitor for 6h, coordinate with Lia to plan customer-facing postmortem and runbook change.

Raj P.: Ack. I'll take on-call. I'll keep the pin for the window and start ticket ENG-RUNTIME-732 to investigate fallback heuristics.

incidents-bot: Incident resolved -> status: mitigated. Closed for paging. Follow-up ticket: ENG-RUNTIME-732.

Emma (on-call): Closing thread. Will add notes to the incident tracker and link to the customer postmortem once Lia schedules it. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
